Source: James, Witten, Hastie and Tibshirani (2021), ISLR 2e,
section 5.1.2, which states the formula for least squares
linear or polynomial regression.
Hastie, Tibshirani and Friedman (2009), ESL 2e, section 7.10.1,
states the same identity for many linear fitting methods.
Checked numerically in @exm-loocv-shortcut.
-->
:::{#thm-loocv-shortcut}
#### Leave-one-out cross-validation for least squares

For a linear model fitted by [ordinary least squares](correlation-regression.qmd#def-ols)
with every [leverage](#def-leverage) $\lev{i} < 1$,
the [leave-one-out estimate](#def-loocv)
can be computed from the single fit to all $n$ observations,
from its [prediction errors](estimation.qmd#def-prediction-error)
$\prederr_i = \fitted_i - y_i$ and its leverages:

$$
\cvest{n} = \frac{1}{n} \sumin \sqf{\frac{\prederr_i}{1 - \lev{i}}}.
$$ {#eq-loocv-shortcut}

:::

::: proof
See @james2021islr2e [sec. 5.1.2]
and @hastie2009elements [sec. 7.10.1];
@rem-loocv-shortcut-proof says why it is not derived here.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-loocv-shortcut-proof}
#### Why the shortcut is cited rather than derived

The derivation needs a formula for how the inverse of the matrix $A$ of @def-leverage
changes when one observation's outer product $\soprod{\vxi}$ is removed from it
(the Sherman--Morrison formula),
which this page does not develop.
@exm-loocv-shortcut checks @eq-loocv-shortcut numerically instead,
against refitting the model $n$ times.

:::
